description: Bomi Kim and colleagues publish a CPU version of the H12 two-dimensional urban flood model. Zenodo lists public Fortran 90 source, a four-metre Portland sample input, CPU and GPU result outputs, and runtime logs under CC BY 4.0. The described implementation uses MPI and OpenMP; the associated manuscript evaluates a separate GPU-hybrid configuration. This model can simulate rainfall-driven surface inundation and compare runtime choices across spatial resolutions. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this H12 release. Benchmark areas are Portland, Oregon, and a downstream Han River basin in Korea, with different domain sizes and grid spacing. A limitation is that the deposited source is the CPU version, while the GPU outputs are comparison evidence, not proof that GPU code is included. Hydraulic calibration, boundary conditions and hardware effects cannot be established from the abstract alone. No archive was downloaded, no flood map was recalculated and no runtime claim was independently tested.
